title: Asha's pea plant cross
body: Asha, a Class 10 student, carried out a breeding experiment with garden pea plants in her school garden. In pea plants, tallness (T) is dominant over shortness (t), and violet flower colour (W) is dominant over white flower colour (w). She took a tall pea plant bearing violet flowers, whose genetic make-up she did not know, and crossed it with a short pea plant bearing white flowers. She collected the seeds, grew them, and recorded the progeny. Out of 120 progeny plants, all 120 bore violet flowers. However, 58 of the plants were tall and 62 were short. Asha's teacher asked her to use Mendel's rules to work out what the genetic make-up of the tall, violet-flowered parent must have been, and to predict what would have happened with a parent of a different genetic make-up.
